svg.title: SAIF threat model: OWASP AI threats mapped to AI system components
svg.desc: Vector redraw of Fig. 2 from the OWASP AI Testing Guide (CC BY-SA 4.0), based on Google's Secure AI Framework (SAIF), with a key to the threat codes.
svg.text: OWASP Top 10 for LLM and AI Exchange threats
mapped to the components of a SAIF baseline architecture
Every tag reads T01-<code>. The grey line under each entry is the OWASP Top 10 for LLM (2025) or OWASP AI Exchange item it maps to.
User-typed instructions override the system prompt
Hidden instructions arrive via pages, files or tool results
Crafted inputs slip past filters and mislead the model
Unsanitised output enables XSS, SSRF or injection downstream
An agent or plugin acts beyond its intended scope
Confident but false or fabricated output
Malicious training data plants bias or backdoors
Poisoned feedback or logs are reused for fine-tuning
Live inference data (RAG, caches, memory) is tampered with
Compromised third-party weights, libraries or frameworks
Manipulated embeddings or vector stores skew retrieval
Cloning a model by systematically querying it
Weights exfiltrated from memory or serving hosts
Model assets stolen from dev pipelines or repositories
AI Exchange 3.2.2 (MTDD in the guide text)
Output reveals PII, secrets or internal data
One user's input surfaces in another user's session
Hidden system instructions exposed in responses
The model reproduces memorised raw training data
Inferring or reconstructing training data from outputs
Indirect or optional flow (agents, external sources, usage data)
SAIF component number, referenced in the guide’s threat scenarios
Adapted from Fig. 2 of the OWASP AI Testing Guide (github.com/OWASP/www-project-ai-testing-guide), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0; architecture based on Google’s Secure AI Framework (SAIF).
This redraw is shared under the same CC BY-SA 4.0 licence. Input Handling (7) lists AIE twice in the original; it appears once here.
